record.file_problem: Repository metadata, README, and file list only; notebook and PDF were not read or run.
record.tranche_reason: Reports a difference-in-means refusal direction and behavioral effects from runtime steering, but intervenes at one layer rather than projecting the direction out of every layer and position.
record.gate_note: The README reports an unsteered and two steered outputs for one adversarial SQL-injection prompt. The layer-wise separation result is used to select Layer 19 and is not recorded as a row. No results are reported for harmless prompts, general capabilities, a weight edit, or training against ablation.
record.test_reason: The study computes a harmful-minus-benign difference-in-means direction in Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct. It then reports what happens to refusal when that direction is subtracted or added at Layer 19. This is a different intervention from the original's all-layer directional ablation, but it asks the same question as V1.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The README claims the steering 'proves that a single 1D direction governs refusal'. It says subtracting the direction gives complete safety ablation and adding it hardens guardrails against prompt injection. The shown evidence does not back the hardening/defense claim: the unsteered model already refuses that prompt, and no successful injection is shown being neutralized.
record.recipe_differences: The README computes a normalized harmful-minus-benign mean-activation direction, but steers at Layer 19 rather than projecting the direction out of every layer and position. This is a repository presenting an interactive reproduction notebook; the notebook was not inspected or run.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported behavioral intervention is at Layer 19; no comparison of behavioral outcomes across layers is reported.
record.problems: The reported behavioral benchmark is a single adversarial prompt with example outputs, with no uncertainty estimates or general-capability evaluation. The notebook and technical report are listed but were not read or run.
record.rows_left_out: No eligible reported behavioral results left out. The README's layer-wise separation and Layer 19 peak are used to select the intervention layer, so are not recorded as rows.

untested.parts: Induction of refusal on harmless prompts; preservation of other capabilities; ablation across all layers and positions; any refusal rate over a prompt set; other models.
No analysis of whether jailbreaks suppress the direction; no training against ablation. The 'defense' claim is not shown, because the baseline already refuses.

missing.what: Contents of the technical report and notebook. These may include results over prompt sets, harmless-prompt induction, or capability checks, none of which were read.

record.verdict_notes: Repository README only; single-prompt demonstrations with no quantitative refusal rates. The Layer-19 relative separation (0.4349) is used to select the layer and is correctly not recorded as a row. The repository creation date (2026) is noted as given.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test projection at every layer and position, refusal on harmless requests after addition, or whether other capabilities remain intact.
No weight edit or released-model abliteration result is reported.
Does not test attacks that suppress the direction or training against its ablation.
Does not compare a single direction with an affine, cone, or multiple-direction account.
Does not separately measure harmfulness judgment and refusal decision.
No transfer across languages, model variants, or base and instruct models is reported.
Does not vary refusal training or training stage.

rows.subject: Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct
rows.operation_detail: Unsteered baseline output on an adversarial SQL-injection prompt
rows.note: The benchmark gives a refusal as the unsteered baseline.
rows.check: Control row: the unsteered baseline refuses. The state just records that a baseline refusal exists; it is not itself evidence for V1.

rows.subject: Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct
rows.operation_detail: Negative runtime steering along the refusal direction at Layer 19
rows.value: Full jailbreak bypass; the model provides an SQL-injection script example
rows.locator: README, Key Empirical Findings and Causal Intervention Benchmark
rows.note: The README describes this as safety ablation. The result is for one adversarial prompt and a one-layer runtime intervention.
rows.check: Linkage and state are fine. Evidence is a single adversarial prompt with one example output, at one layer, with a tuned alpha=-1.5 and gamma=0.4. There is no prompt set and no rate.

rows.subject: Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct
rows.operation_detail: Positive runtime steering along the refusal direction at Layer 19
rows.locator: README, Key Empirical Findings and Causal Intervention Benchmark
rows.note: The prompt is adversarial and harmful, not harmless; this result does not establish the claimed induction of refusals to harmless requests.
rows.check: The baseline already refuses, so adding the direction cannot show induced refusal. It also cannot show the claimed defense against prompt injection, because no bypass existed to neutralize. No harmless prompt was tested.

relationships.condition: Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct; subtracting the direction at Layer 19 (alpha=-1.5, gamma=0.4); one adversarial SQL-injection prompt
relationships.reason: The unsteered model refuses (R1), while negative steering produces a compliant SQL-injection script (R2). This is anecdotal: one prompt, no rate.
relationships.display_finding: The unsteered model refused the adversarial prompt, while subtracting the direction produced a compliant SQL-injection script.
